newsitem.title: PERU: Avalanche in Peru Andes leaves two dead, 13 missing.
newsitem.headline: Avalanche in Peru Andes leaves two dead, 13 missing.

text.p: An avalanche crashed onto a campsite on Peru's highest peak, Huascaran, killing a Peruvian guide and French trekker and leaving 13 others missing, mountaineers and rescue workers said on Monday.

The avalanche hit the hikers early on Saturday at a rest area known as Camp 2, some 13,800 feet (4,200 meters) up the 22,100-foot (6,700 meters) snow-covered mountain in Peru's northern Ancash district.

Carlos Paredes, spokesman for the civil defence in the nearby town of Huaraz, said a helicopter was on its way to the zone Monday morning to search for the missing walkers, believed to include Peruvians, North Americans and Europeans.

"From what we've heard, when the avalanche came down, they abandoned the tents and just ran," said Huaraz adventure tour operator Lourdes Foronda Valverde. "Two of them were covered, while the others apparently got away."
Paredes added that another four people disappeared Saturday in an avalance at another mountain in the zone. But he could not give more details.
Ancash, which includes the towering Cordillera Blanca or "White Range" of mountains, is one of Peru's most popular tourist regions.
